threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot the newcomers by their confusion over whether to queue for the bus or just wave it down like it’s a taxi. Proper bus etiquette takes time.
Caught a night bus from Brixton last week; the driver was blasting old reggae. Half the bus was singing along, felt like a block party on wheels.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I heard a toddler arguing passionately with their parent about whether the garbage truck was a 'big truck' or a 'huge truck'—that's Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can spot spontaneous dance parties in the subway stations here. Just last week, a group broke out into a conga line at Kottbusser Tor.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You notice the locals look up when the BART screeches—it's a weird instinct. Those just visiting jump at the noise like it's the first time.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo get on the 14. He looked like he had just come from a wedding, but spent the whole ride checking his phone like he was in a board meeting.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia’s plazas are just for tapas and photos, but locals know they’re real community hubs come dusk, filled with laughter and life.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they still look at the metro map like it’s a treasure map—lost in the maze of lines and colors.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think a '5-minute stroll' means a straight line to the pub, not a detour through three pop-up coffee shops and a market.
Caught a bloke in a three-piece suit arguing with a tree at the bus stop last night. Felt like I was in a surreal play, but he seemed dead serious.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Hearing the late-night kebab orders mixing with the sound of street musicians, I realized Berlin's heartbeat is just outside my window.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do they turn a street party into a pop-up park; they bring in real grass, benches, and DJ decks. It's like a mini-festival for a weekend.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their reaction to a BART delay—most just sigh and roll their eyes, while newcomers start looking for rideshare apps.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, saw a guy serenading the Muni crowd with an old guitar, while a raccoon rummaged through a trash can nearby. Classic SF vibe.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think plaça del Sol is just for sunbathing, but locals use it for evening hangouts and impromptu concerts. Totally different vibe.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at how cut-off the metro is during major events. That deer-in-headlights look by the travel maps says it all.
